messages:
sam: heads up — after the continuous-batching change we rolled last night I'm seeing a big divergence between token latency and prefix cache hit-rate. p99 increased and cache hit-rate tanked on a few routes. :frowning_face:
priya: ugh. which routes and what numbers?
sam: route: /v1/chat/generate (default model pool). baseline (before change): cache hit-rate ~78%, median latency ~65ms, p99 ~190ms. after: hit-rate ~49%, median latency ~82ms, p99 ~320ms. throughput similar but token cost up ~18%.
marco: do we have a trace that shows why hit-rate dropped? could be keying mismatch or batch composition mixing new prefixes into KV shards.
sam: yup. I profiled a few requests — the batch composer is aggregating by arrival window only, so sometimes a short-request with same prefix sits in a batch with long-seq items. That changes the per-request kernel path because we switch to long-seq attention kernels for the whole batch, and also we evict/overwrite shared kv keys more aggressively.
alice: can you paste the profiler output? especially kernel selection and kv ops.
sam: pasted below:
```
PROFILE: request 0 (short, prefix A) -> selected kernel: multihead_attn_v2_long_seq (latency 22ms)
KV: load key A found=false (miss)
PROFILE: request 1 (long, prefix B) -> selected kernel: multihead_attn_v2_long_seq (latency 85ms)
KV: load key B found=true
BATCH_COMPOSER: merged requests 0,1 into batch size=2 window=12ms
RESULT: request 0 ended up with miss, warmup of KV started but not complete -> extra tokens produced -> final latency 140ms
```
priya: hmm so short prefix A used to hit cached KV if isolated, but being merged causes eviction/overwrites? sounds like our KV key namespace is sensitive to sequence-length-dependent placement.
marco: is the keying scheme including sequence length or some batch metadata? that'd be bad.
sam: no, keying is currently: sha256(prefix_text + model_id + param_version) — stable. but the runtime shards keys across GPU instances based on a placement hash that uses sample-length histogram to balance hot keys. after the batching change the distribution shifted and hot keys ended up scattered, increasing remote reads and misses.
alice: so root cause: batch composition changed request distributions that the placement hash wasn't robust to. placement relied on our older per-minute length histogram, now live mixing breaks assumptions.
nate: any quick mitigations? can we pin hot prefixes to single shard or add a TTL-based local cache bypass for very short prefixes?
priya: two practical ideas: (1) pin top-N prefixes (by freq) to a local KV shard in-memory (very fast lookup), (2) introduce a tiny prefetch/warmup micro-batch for newly seen prefixes before merging them with arbitrary requests.
marco: idea (2) sounds promising: when a short prefix arrives and is cold, spawn a micro-warmup batch of size up to 4 with only that prefix (or similar ones) and complete warmup before routing to the general composer. This costs extra ops but preserves hit-rate for tail latency-sensitive requests.
sam: I simulated a 10k request trace with that prewarm micro-batch: hit-rate recovered to 73%, p99 dropped from 320ms to ~210ms, extra GPU cycles +4%.
priya: nice. we should also change placement to be less sensitive to instantaneous sequence-length skew. maybe use a stable consistent hash independent of seq length and then rebalance during low-load.
alice: agree. Also adding metrics: per-prefix hit-rate, per-shard remote-read-rate, and batch-composition histograms (fraction of batches with mixed-length requests).
perf-bot: perf-bot: regression detected on /v1/chat/generate on 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC -> p99 latency +68%, cache hit-rate -29%. Ticket: PERF-4321
sam: opened PERF-4321 and added simulation results + micro-warmup patch.
marco: low-risk rollout plan:
- Stage 1: enable micro-warmup in staging for top 100 prefixes, measure hit-rate and extra cycles (2 days)
- Stage 2: fade-in micro-warmup for latency-sensitive routes with feature flag (1 week)
- Stage 3: deploy placement refactor to consistent-hash (canary small fleet)
- Stage 4: full rollout + add observability dashboards
priya: also let's add an integration test: synthetic workload that mixes short+long seqs at high conc and assert no hit-rate drop >5% after composer changes. put this in eng-runtime CI.
alice: good. one more thought — kernel selection changes are also inflating latency. can we attempt dynamic per-request kernel override if batch contains heterogeneous lengths? e.g., split batch into sub-batches by seq length if mixing cost outweighs batching benefit.
marco: that would increase scheduling complexity but might be worth it. we can heuristically split batches if estimated p99 for mixed batch > threshold. Need cost model.
nate: I'll start a small experiment to estimate cost model: build estimator E(batch) = expected_latency_savings_if_split - overhead_of_additional_kernels. use past traces to fit.
sam: thanks. action items: 1) priya/infra do placement change design, 2) marco implement micro-warmup prototype, 3) nate build cost estimator, 4) alice add dashboards + CI test, 5) I'll coordinate rollout docs for PERF-4321.
priya: assigning tasks in linear and slack threads. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: created canary job run/rv-2026-03-11-09 
sam: thanks all. we'll sync tomorrow in standup if anyone has blockers. :eyes:
